title: The red-first proof is timed and costs one run, not three
description: Design: quality-gates-internal plans/2026-11-27-speed-red-first.md. Paid probe on c4ee25b8: after every writer round the red-first proof took 334-335 s of untimed wall (three sweeps of the task's test file), 40.9% of the gap to plain; a re-gate after a one-suite red ran that suite alone and again inside the full gate (+112 s).
desiredOutcome: The drive attributes the red-first proof as its own timed stage, reuses a leg whose inputs did not change, leaves the fix leg to the green task gate, and a re-gate after a one-suite red costs no more than the first gate; measured by the next probe's stage breakdown

findings.issue: On the Agent route the drive counts submit's proof time twice. agent_stage records the executor's `writer` stage from the hand-out to the filed return (the journal row submit writes after red_block). note_proof_stage then adds a separate `proof` stage for a run that falls inside that window. _task_timing.summarize adds both kinds into attributedMs and does not read the basis, so the proof's milliseconds are counted twice. A submit that is refused and then retried adds one more inside stage per attempt. overrunMs only shows this when the stages add up to more than the window. Otherwise unattributedMs is silently understated by the proof length, and the per-kind totals in /audit:status overstate the work. The basis sentence admits the overlap, but no reader of the summary reads the basis. The executor's outcome says 'summarize reports it as overrun there'; that is true only in the case where the stages exceed the window.
findings.resolution: Make the figures add up. Option one: when queue_agent_stage builds the executor's writer stage, subtract the proof stages noted for this start whose startedAt falls in [hand-out, filed], and say the subtraction in the writer stage's basis. Option two: have submit pass its proof length through the filed return so the drive can split the writer stage into writer and proof. Add a pq case in which a handed-out Agent writer whose submit noted a proof gets writer.ms + proof.ms equal to the hand-out-to-filing length, not more.

findings.issue: A leg is listed as `ran: true` with `seconds: 0.0` when _isolated_run returned before starting the command: no time left, a failed reset or unlink, or a failed dependency link. The drive's proof_legs_said then prints 'task 0.00 s' without the leg's problem. That is the 'missing leg read as a leg of no time' that the red_legs docstring and the guide paragraph say cannot happen.
findings.resolution: In red_legs, list a record whose code is None and whose problem is set as `ran: false` with that problem as `why`. Alternatively, have proof_legs_said add a ran leg's `problem` when one is present.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "a gate that does not name them runs the fix leg as today": the fix leg runs as today, but its outcome is handled differently. Before this change a writer's first proof whose fix leg could not prove was held by prove_and_hold, which refuses only when was == proved, and was filed honestly as could-not-prove. Causes include a fix-run timeout, a start_problem budget, fix_problem's collected-count check, and a throwaway missing an ignored build output or an undeclared file. Now the first proof is a by-gate `proved` that made no fix run. When gate_binding fails (for example a runner printing no paths, so coverage is None), fix_leg_proof gets could-not-prove and returns red_refused. That is red-refused-writer, which sends the writer session a timeout or environment reason it cannot fix, for up to MAX_RESUME_ROUNDS, then red-refused. The held by-gate proof stays, so every later filing repeats the fallback. A return that used to file now never files. No fbg case covers a non-proved fallback.
findings.resolution: In fix_leg_proof, hold and file a non-proved fallback block the way prove_and_hold treats a first proof: hold the could-not-prove block and let file_writer_return file it, with the binding failure added to the basis. Keep red_refused only for a helper refusal or a block that no longer shows red. Add an fbg case where the fallback helper answers could-not-prove and assert that exactly one return is filed with that status.

findings.issue: A by-gate proof is now filed carrying an implementationDigest that can name bytes other than the ones it is filed with. The helper still computes implementationDigest under --fix-by-gate (stamp-verification.py:4621), and writer_prove puts it on the block (5790-5792). tree_since_proof now ignores implementation drift for such a proof. Example: a resume round changes only src/mine.py and the gate names the test file. The binding holds, nothing re-proves, and the filed redFirst.implementationDigest is round 0's. The comments on file_writer_return ("a return is filed only with a proof made over the HEAD and the declared test and implementation files it is filed with") and the module docstring's THE INVARIANT ("a HEAD or a declared file that moved is proved again before anything is filed") are now false for this path, and neither was updated. That leaves a false statement in committed evidence and in the code's own invariant prose.
findings.resolution: When filing a bound by-gate block, drop implementationDigest, which no fix run of this proof read, or replace it with the digest of the declared implementation as the bound gate ran it. Reword the module docstring at ~215-225 and the THE INVARIANT comment in file_writer_return to exempt a fix-by-gate proof's implementation half, as execute-task.md's drift paragraph now does. Add a case on the bound path where only the implementation moved, and assert what the filed block says about the implementation.

findings.issue: gate_binding stands in for the helper's fix leg with a weaker check, and the filed basis does not say so. It reads the run-wide `observations.coverage`, which run-test-gate builds from the output text of every step (run-test-gate.py:5812, 5858), plus the run's `passed` status. It never checks that the step running the proof's own command (writer_test_command, the red_command entry) ran in that run. task_gate_steps drops entries matching executor.phaseGateOnly, and red_command does not consult that setting. A test entry left to the phase gate can therefore be absent from the bound run while another step (a lint or typecheck printing the path) makes coverage name the test file, and the block is filed `proved` and bound to a run that never ran the test. The binding also skips fix_problem's collected-count and per-file sweep-count checks, which caught a red case that went missing (skipped or deselected) rather than passing. Meanwhile the basis claims a "green run of these tests on the working tree".
findings.resolution: Bind only when the run's step whose resolved command equals the proof's command is present, measured (not left out), passed, and itself named the test file. Use the row's per-step data, or the step text run-test-gate keeps. When that step is absent, fall back to fix_leg_proof. Optionally compare the step's collected count with the task leg's collected count, as fix_problem does. Add an fbg case: coverage names the test file through another step while the proof's step is absent, and assert the fallback.

findings.issue: testsAdded names the fg6-fg8 cases in tests/test_stamp_verification.py, but casesAdded binds only fbg1-fbg9, so the stamp-verification cases are not bound for case grading.
findings.resolution: Add a casesAdded entry for fg6-fg8 on the next filing.

tasks.description: Design: quality-gates-internal plans/2026-11-27-speed-red-first.md section 2, T6. outcome.technical: MEASUREMENT FIRST (it decides the task). Two pristine `git archive HEAD` exports in scratch, `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_stamp_verification.py` (391 cases). Run 1: one alone 26.9 s, two at once 32.9 s wall (1.22x). Then a 150 s gap. Run 2: one alone 27.0 s, two at once 33.6 s (1.24x). Both under the 1.4x bar, so the task went ahead. Host: darwin with 10 cpus; the 1-minute load average was 15.0 just before run 1 and 9.8-12.4 after the pairs, while a sibling executor ran. IMPLEMENTATION (stamp-verification.py): new `_concurrent_legs(aside, here)` runs the baseline leg on a thread and the task leg on the main thread. `_run_in`, `_timed_run` and `_isolated_run` gain an optional `started` callback, which hands the baseline's process back so that on an interrupt or error the main thread tears its group down with `_proc_group.tear_down`, also tears down any process started after that, joins the thread, and raises again. An error raised in the thread is raised again in the main thread. `run_red` builds two throwaways (two holders, each with its own OWNER_FILE, so `leftover_throwaways` needs no change); each is built lazily under a lock, because two `git worktree add` calls at once raced: one run failed with 'failed to read .git/worktrees/tree/commondir', and the lock fixed it. The `_run_in`/`_isolated_run` stand-ins accept `started`. `_signal_mid_run` records every pid and kills all of them after SIGKILL; before that change, two hold processes from my own sweeps were left running, and I killed both by pid.
